payload.claim: Acceptance criterion 3 requires that `ready_task` recognize a pool-cut probe entry 'whose error is the text review._review_pool_cut writes', but `_rt_pool_cut_entry` hand-types that text instead of calling `review._review_pool_cut`, and no test anywhere calls `_pool_cut_witness` against the real function's output. Changing review.py's wording (e.g. 'never started' to 'did not run') breaks the real pool-cut detection in `ready_task` silently (every genuinely cut probe/wrong-version session would then be missed, wrongly admitting an ORPHANED task whose review was actually incomplete), yet this whole test file stays green because its fixture duplicates the old wording rather than deriving it from the source function. The gap is exactly what the criterion's own text calls out and no test closes it.
